properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued September 5 at 3:24AM CDT by NWS Bismarck ND
properties.description:
At 324 AM CDT, a strong thunderstorm was located 6 miles south of
Flaxton, or 35 miles north of Stanley, moving northeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Bowbells, Flaxton, Coteau, and Northgate.
properties.instruction:
Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued September 5 at 4:24AM EDT by NWS Wilmington OH
properties.description:
At 424 AM EDT, strong thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from 6 miles north of St. Paris to 6 miles east of West
Mansfield, moving southeast at 55 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 45 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Hail may cause minor damage to
vegetation.

Locations impacted include...
Delaware, Marysville, Sidney, Bellefontaine, Urbana, Richwood, St.
Paris, West Liberty, North Lewisburg, De Graff, West Mansfield,
Radnor, Milford Center, Quincy, Ostrander, Christiansburg, Fletcher,
Port Jefferson, Woodstock, and Magnetic Springs.

This includes I-75 in Ohio between mile markers 89 and 94.

If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a sturdy building.

A Severe Thunderstorm Watch remains in effect until 800 AM EDT for
central and west central Ohio.

To report hazardous weather conditions, go to our website at
weather.gov/iln and submit your report via social media, when you can
do so safely.

properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 5 at 3:19AM CDT until September 5 at 3:45AM CDT by NWS Sioux Falls SD
properties.description:
At 319 AM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Ethan, or 10
miles northeast of Parkston, moving east at 15 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

southwestern Hanson and north central Hutchinson Counties.
properties.instruction:

building.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued September 5 at 4:04AM EDT until September 5 at 7:00AM EDT by NWS Wilmington OH
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southwestern Union County in central Ohio...
Northeastern Champaign County in west central Ohio...
Eastern Logan County in west central Ohio...

* WHEN...Until 700 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 404 AM EDT, radar and automated rain gauges indicated heavy
rain due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2.5 inches
of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 1.5
inches are possible.
- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Marysville, Plain City, North Lewisburg, West Mansfield,
Northwood, Milford Center, Rushsylvania, Woodstock, Unionville
Center, Valley Hi, Zanesfield, Pottersburg, Middleburg, East
Liberty, Raymond, Pickrelltown, Mingo, Broadway and New
Jerusalem.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

To report flooding, go to our website at weather.gov/iln and submit
your report via social media, when you can do so safely.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued September 5 at 3:34AM EDT until September 5 at 6:30AM EDT by NWS Wilmington OH
properties.description:
FFWILN

The National Weather Service in Wilmington has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Logan County in west central Ohio...

* Until 630 AM EDT.

* At 334 AM EDT, radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts
of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Bellefontaine, West Liberty, Russells Point, Lakeview, Huntsville,
Valley Hi, Zanesfield, Mcmorran, New Jerusalem, Pickrelltown,
Lewistown, East Liberty and Middleburg.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

To report flash flooding, go to our website at weather.gov/iln and
submit your report via social media, when you can do so safely.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Menard Creek near Rye affecting Liberty, Hardin and Polk Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...Menard Creek near Rye.

* WHEN...Until Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 23.0 feet, Moderate lowland flooding begins as
low-lying areas along the creek are inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:15 PM CDT Friday the stage was 21.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 17.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:15 PM CDT Friday was 28.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage after
midnight and continue a gradual fall.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 21.5
feet on 06/27/1999.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
